newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran raises fuel prices on Saturday to cut subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Iran raises fuel prices on Saturday to cut subsidies.

text.p: Iran is to raise the retail prices of refined oil products on Saturday as part of measures to reduce heavy state subsidies for fuel.

State-run Tehran radio said on Friday the price of regular and lead-free gasolines would increase to 160 rials (5.3 U.S. cents) from 130 rials per litre while premium petrol would be raised 40 rials to 220 rials a litre.

It said the yearly step, in line with a parliamentary decree in 1994 to reduce subsidies during the country's second five year plan (1995-2000), would also raise kerosene and diesel prices by 10 rials to 40 rials a litre.
Fuel oil would be lifted five rials to 20 rials, it added.
Similar increases last year lead to public criticism of the government by media and residents.

Oil ministry officials have warned that subsidies have made prices for oil products in Iran some of the cheapest in the world, encouraging inefficient energy use, runaway demand and smuggling of fuel to neighbouring countries.

Though Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter -- selling some 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude -- it has on occasion imported some oil products, such as gasoline, to meet local demand.
Some officials have warned that Iran's position as an oil exporter could be threatened if domestic demand is not curtailed. ($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
